title: Step 7 static-validation report
description: Structured report written by mellea_skills_compiler.compile.lints.run_lints() after the Step 7 lint suite runs. Persisted at <package>/intermediate/step_7_report.json. Consumed by the repair loop (compile/mellea_skills.py::_lint_repair_retry_loop), the F1 prescription builder (compile/repair_prompt.py::build_repair_prompt_lint_section), and any CI tooling that gates on lint outcomes. The writer currently emits a flat `lints` array with no tier nesting; tier membership is recoverable from `_LINT_TIER` in compile/lints.py.

format_version.description: Frozen at 1.1 (the format that introduced per-lint severity). Bump when the report shape changes in a way consumers must adapt to.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp recorded when run_lints() finished.

package_path.description: Path string identifying the package the lints ran against. Typically a directory name relative to the skill root (e.g. 'ticket_triage_mellea/'); the writer does not normalise it.

overall_verdict.description: 'fail' iff at least one entry in `lints` has `verdict == "fail"` AND its effective severity is `error`. WARNING-severity and INFO-severity failures are surfaced in this report but do NOT flip the verdict (unless strict mode escalated them — see `effective_severity` on individual entries).

warnings.description: Count of `lints` entries with `verdict == "fail"` AND `severity == "warning"`. Independent of whether `--strict` promoted them; the raw count is what's reported.

info_failures.description: Count of `lints` entries with `verdict == "fail"` AND `severity == "info"`. Strict mode does NOT promote these.

strict.description: True when run_lints() was invoked with strict=True (`mellea-skills compile|validate --strict`). When true, WARNING-severity failures are promoted to blocking — observable via `effective_severity` on the affected entries.

smoke_check_mode.description: The --smoke-check mode the run was invoked with. Recorded for replay. Optional in the writer's emitted shape if the run never reached smoke-check (e.g. early lint halt).

warnings_escalated_by_smoke.description: Lint ids whose WARNING-severity failures were promoted to blocking *for this run* because the smoke-check independently confirmed the failure path (e.g. a `complex-schema-needs-strategy-or-fallback` warning whose fixture hit the missing-strategy crash). Each affected entry in `lints` will carry `effective_severity == "error"`.

verdict.description: Outcome of the Step 7b fixture smoke-check. `passed` = ran to completion; `failed` = raised a real exception; `skipped` = backend unreachable (ConnectionError/TimeoutError/auth failure) — does NOT flip overall_verdict.

fixture_used.description: ID of the fixture from `<package>/fixtures/__init__.py:ALL_FIXTURES` that was exercised. `null` when verdict is `skipped` before any fixture loaded.

duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock seconds for the fixture run, or null when the run never started.

backend_available.description: True if the LLM backend responded before timeout. False on `skipped`-due-to-unreachable verdicts.

skipped_reason.description: Short reason string when verdict is `skipped`; null otherwise. Examples: 'backend unreachable', 'authentication failed (check API key or env vars)'.

error.description: Short error class + message when verdict is `failed`; null on pass/skip. Full traceback lives in intermediate/step_7b_report.json (sibling artifact).

smoke_check.description: Smoke-check sub-report. Null when smoke-check did not run for this invocation (e.g. --no-run, or static lints failed before smoke-check would have been reached).

lints.description: One entry per lint that ran. The writer emits a flat array — no tier nesting. Consumers that want to group by tier should join against `_LINT_TIER` in compile/lints.py.

lint_id.description: Stable identifier; matches a key in `_LINT_SEVERITY` / `_LINT_TIER` in compile/lints.py.

verdict.description: Per-lint outcome. `pass` = no failures; `fail` = failures collected; `warning` = lint flagged a non-blocking issue (rare — most warnings come via severity, not verdict); `skipped` = lint declined to run (missing inputs, not-applicable to this package shape, etc.). See `skipped_reason` for the explanation.

effective_severity.description: Severity *as applied to overall_verdict for this run*. Equal to `severity` in normal mode. Equal to `error` when (a) the run was strict and `severity == warning`, or (b) the lint id is in `warnings_escalated_by_smoke`. Optional — older writers may omit it; consumers should fall back to `severity` when absent.

files_checked.description: Number of source files the lint inspected. Zero is valid (e.g. when the lint scope was vacuous on this package).

skipped_reason.description: Human-readable reason when `verdict == "skipped"`. Null when the lint actually ran.

file.description: Relative path from the package root (e.g. 'pipeline.py', 'fixtures/test_happy_path.py').

line.description: 1-indexed line number; null when the failure is whole-file (e.g. missing file, top-level config drift).

column.description: 1-indexed column number; null when the failure has no precise column position.

message.description: What's wrong and what to do about it. Should be self-contained — operators may read it without opening the source.

rule_ref.description: Optional pointer to the rule being enforced. Format is free-form today: KB ids (`KB 5`), spec rules (`R-SEM-SIGNATURE-MATCH`), document references (`mellea-fy-validate.md § Tier 2 — session-boundary`).
